questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a millionaire before the age of forty
Planning your money for the lifestyle you want
How to find a better-paid job in the city
Why young people spend too much on clothes and phones
questions.why: Neil says they're talking about finance and planning for future lifestyles.

questions.q: How many numbers does Julie Lord say you need to start?
options: Two
Three
Four
Six
questions.why: She says, 'You just need four numbers.'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Julie Lord's numbers?
options: Your income
What you own
What you owe
Your age
questions.why: The four are income, expenditure, assets and liabilities.

questions.q: What does the cashflow forecast show you?
options: Your future lifestyle, with or without financial products
How much income tax you must pay this year and next
Which bank gives the best interest on your savings
How much your house is worth today on the market
questions.why: She says they project forward to show what lifestyle you'll have if you do nothing, or use products.

questions.q: How does Rob keep track of his money?
options: He doesn't keep track at all and hopes for the best
He uses a detailed spreadsheet of income and spending
A financial planner does it all for him every month
He writes it down in a notebook once every year
questions.why: He says he has a very detailed spreadsheet listing his income and expenditure.

questions.q: How does Rob feel when he looks at his spreadsheet?
options: Proud of how much he has saved so far
Excited about his plans for the future
A bit depressed about how little he has
Confused by all the numbers and columns
questions.why: He says it reminds him how much money he doesn't have: 'It's quite depressing!'

questions.q: What is Neil's attitude to his own finances?
options: He is very organised and checks them each week
He worries about them every day and can't sleep
He has a good pension plan and plenty of savings
He doesn't know his debts and tries not to worry
questions.why: He says he lives in 'blissful ignorance' and has no idea how big his debts are.

questions.q: What does Julie Lord say about her younger clients?
options: They want help getting organised and understanding products
They are only interested in pensions and retirement
They are much richer than her older clients
She doesn't have any clients under the age of fifty
questions.why: She says many younger clients want to get financially organised and understand the products.
